title: Is GPT-5's Low CoT Controllability Consistent Across Model Sizes?
original_idea: Measure CoT controllability using OpenAI's forbidden-word methodology on GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, and replicate with Llama 3.1 at multiple sizes. Plot controllability vs. scale.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The exact research question (CoT controllability vs. model size) has been answered by OpenAI's CoT-Control paper with open-source code and comprehensive results across multiple model families.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Forbidden-word methodology is straightforward but running Llama at multiple sizes requires local GPU setup. API models are easier. Mixed accessibility.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing across 6+ model sizes/families is broad. Running Llama locally at large scales needs significant compute time. Hard to complete in 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: OpenAI's 'Reasoning Models Struggle to Control Their Chains of Thought' (arxiv 2603.05706, March 2026) directly answers this question. The paper tests CoT controllability across frontier models including GPT-5.2 Thinking, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and two families of open-weight models at multiple sizes. Key finding: controllability is higher for larger models but decreases with post-training and longer reasoning. Scores range from 0.1% to 15.4% across all frontier models tested. The CoT-Control evaluation suite is open-source with 13,000+ tasks. This idea has been fully executed and published.
